top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single, well-defined invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) taken from concept to record 1e-18 accuracy and already used in geodesy and constants tests. The Katori and Ye allocation is clean and fits the statute, and a citation limited to the lattice clock stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. The overlap and omitted contributors are real but are handled by careful wording, so an award is preferable to no award.
